subject: Request: availability variance annex + evidence for MSA/order form
messages:
From: Rachel Cheng <rachel.cheng@meditech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@meditech.com>; ops@meditech.com
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability variance annex + evidence request

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the team at MediTech is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we finalize an order form, Procurement needs a proposed addendum for one availability variance we discussed: a regional uptime exception for our on-prem routed traffic during major patch windows (up to 1% monthly deviation) and a P95 latency commitment for inference under dedicated capacity.

Can you provide: 
- Draft language we can insert into the MSA as an "Availability Variance Annex" (short, redline-ready).
- Evidence: 90/95/99 uptime/latency metrics for the last 12 months for the us-west region and a short note on fallback behavior (regional failover + model variant fallback).
- Proposed credit schedule if the monthly availability falls below the proposed threshold.

Procurement would like a single PDF with redlines and a short summary to circulate internally. If possible please also indicate whether this impacts Dedicated pricing or order form language (we may need explicit order form checkbox language).

Appreciate a draft by EOD Friday so we can circulate to Legal.

Best,
Rachel Cheng
Director, Procurement
MediTech Solutions

Attachments: none

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Cheng <rachel.cheng@meditech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability variance annex + evidence request

Rachel — thanks for the clear ask. Labelling the deliverables below so we stay aligned: 

1) Draft annex language (redline and clean) — will attach a Word redline + PDF summary.
2) Evidence package — uptime and latency slices, plus an ops note on fallbacks and expected RTO during cross-region failover.
3) Order form language — proposed checkbox and a short clause that we can add to the Order Form under "Service Commitments" (affects Dedicated only).

Looping in Karthik for the technical appendix and Stephanie for legal/order-form phrasing.

We have internal templates for availability annexes; I can adapt one to explicitly call out the regional variance and credit schedule options (per-month credits tiered by % below threshold). Will send the first draft within 24 hours.

Quick Q: For the P95 latency commitment, do you want it for single-request 1k token inference, or for your typical 90/10 mix? If you can confirm the traffic profile the ops team expects (percent long requests), we can include a tailored metric.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial-availability-annex-template.docx (stub)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Cheng <rachel.cheng@meditech.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability variance annex + evidence request

Rachel / Priyom — attaching a short technical appendix and a proposed credit schedule. High level notes: 

- Fallback behavior: requests routed out-of-region are attempted only if capacity allows; default for Dedicated is model-variant fallback (quantized variant with same topology) before cross-region routing. RTO for cross-region failover is typically 3-7 minutes in our tests; we capture a P95 of 4.2 minutes.
- Uptime: historical us-west monthly availability across Dedicated pools (2027-2028 rolling 12mo) shows 99.995% median; we will attach the sliced spreadsheet.
- Latency: P95 observed for 1k token generation on Dedicated (single request) averaged 270ms over Q1-2028 under standard batching profile; under heavy burst workloads P95 is 420ms.

Proposed credit schedule (draft):
- Availability >= 99.9%: no credit
- 99.0% <= Availability < 99.9%: 5% monthly service credit
- 98.0% <= Availability < 99.0%: 15% monthly service credit
- Availability < 98.0%: 30% monthly service credit + remediation plan requirement

This language is intentionally conservative; if MediTech needs a higher tolerance for maintenance windows (e.g., 1% deviation allowance during scheduled patches) we can add a carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows with advance notice and mitigation steps.

Attaching: uptime-latency-metrics-Q1-2028.xlsx (stubs), tech-appendix-availability.pdf (stub), proposed-availability-redline.docx (stub).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tech-appendix-availability.pdf, proposed-availability-redline.docx, uptime-latency-metrics-Q1-2028.xlsx

From: Rachel Cheng <rachel.cheng@meditech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@meditech.com; ops@meditech.com; karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>; stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability variance annex + evidence request

Thanks Karthik — useful detail. Procurement redlines attached (see redline-availability-annex-v2.pdf). Two specific asks from Legal/Procurement: 

1) Add an explicit carve-out that allows a cumulative 1% per-month variance during scheduled major patch windows, provided Redwood gives 72 hours notice and publishes mitigation steps; procurement wants this as a non-credit exception (i.e., not counted against credits).
2) Clarify that Dedicated pricing remains unchanged for the annex, but that the order form must include a checkbox where the customer accepts the Availability Variance Annex and acknowledges the carve-outs.

Also — can you confirm the maximum single-event outage you have on record in us-west over the last 12 months (we need the worst-case single incident duration to evaluate our SRE risk profile)?

Attached: MediTech_MSA_redlines_2028.pdf (procurement redlines)

If you can send a clean redline and a short cover note for Legal by COB Monday (04/30), we can get this into our internal approval queue.

Best,
Rachel

Attachments: MediTech_MSA_redlines_2028.pdf, redline-availability-annex-v2.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Cheng <rachel.cheng@meditech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability variance annex + evidence request

Rachel — appreciate the quick turn. We can accommodate the 1% scheduled-maintenance carve-out with the 72-hour notice and published mitigation steps; we'll mark it as a non-credit exception in the annex. Karthik — can you add a short clause with the remediation timeline expectations and the single-incident historical max?

Next steps (summary):
- Karthik to insert single-incident worst-case and remediation timeline into the tech appendix (by EOD today).
- Stephanie to produce a clean MSA redline with the carve-out language and an Order Form checkbox snippet.
- I will bundle the clean redline PDF + summary cover note and the evidence spreadsheet and push a DocuSign envelope for acceptance of the Order Form checkbox.

Stephanie / Karthik — please flag any PTO conflicts; Rachel, I’ll send the packet and DocuSign link by Monday morning for your Legal review.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bundle-ready-packet-stub.zip (will contain proposed-availability-redline.docx, clean-msa-redline.pdf, uptime-latency-metrics-Q1-2028.xlsx)
